critical.issue: Documented admin PIN '246810' (from /app/memory/test_credentials.md and backend/.env ADMIN_PIN) returns 401 'Wrong PIN.' against the current DB pin_hash. Verified directly: bcrypt.checkpw('246810', current pin_hash) == False, and bcrypt.checkpw(env ADMIN_PIN, current pin_hash) == False too. This means the PIN was changed via POST /api/admin/pin at some point (likely during a prior testing iteration) and the DB was never restored back to 246810, even though iteration_6.json explicitly claimed 'PIN=246810' was restored. This is UNRELATED to the bot.py drop_pending_updates fix (no code path connects them) but it is a real, currently-blocking issue: the documented admin credentials do not work, so admin login (PUT /api/settings, POST /api/admin/pin) could not be fully exercised. Stopped further PIN guesses after confirming to avoid triggering the 5-attempt brute-force lockout (admin_attempts count is now at 5/5 for the test IP after 2 failed attempts across two test runs -- next wrong attempt will trigger a 15-min lockout).

rca_of_the_issue: bot.py fix RCA: previously drop_pending_updates=True caused python-telegram-bot's Application.run_polling to discard any Telegram updates queued server-side during the brief window the bot process was offline (crash-loop/restart), so /start clicks arriving during that window were silently lost instead of processed on reconnect. Setting drop_pending_updates=False makes the bot fetch and process any updates Telegram queued during the outage once it reconnects, closing the conversion-loss gap. This is verified correct in code and via a clean, stable restart with no crash-loop. The separate PIN issue's RCA: pin_hash in bot_settings diverges from ADMIN_PIN in .env and from the documented test PIN 246810, most likely because a previous testing session called POST /api/admin/pin to change the PIN during test execution and the 'restore' step (claimed in iteration_6.json) did not actually persist back to the original hash before the session ended.
